items.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998
items.q: And Michael Cogswell has done a terrific job as curator of that collection.

ctx.x: Well I’m glad you said that because I keep forgetting to tell people that, when they talk about Louis and being an Uncle Tom and so forth. I’ve said many times, look, that’s the way he was, he loved people. And do you sit down and write long letters to people that you don’t see very often? Well he did it all the time. He wrote letters every day of his life. I’m ashamed to say that I left I think all but one or two of his letters in the files of Columbia Records when I left, and they disappeared or they’re in the…

collectors and I’m happy to say in some cases donated to archives like the Louis Armstrong Archive at Queens College, which is an incredible repository because Armstrong left everything, as a collection, to Queens College to preserve for all time. And Michael Cogswell has done a terrific job as curator of that collection.

Yeah. He must have had an incredible energy also, because I did visit there and when you look at all the things he did with his tapes you know, just decorating the boxes and all that, like he was never without something to do.
